hints: Draw a single linear horizontal axis spanning from at least 4 to 16, and label it 'Time (seconds)'.
Construct the box-and-whisker plot for Girls using the five-figure summary: minimum 5, lower quartile 5.5, median 7, upper quartile 9, and maximum 13.
Construct the box-and-whisker plot for Boys on the same horizontal scale using: minimum 4, lower quartile 6, median 8.5, upper quartile 11, and maximum 16.
Label each plot clearly with 'Girls' and 'Boys'.
walkthrough:
Draw a shared linear horizontal axis with an even scale covering the entire range from $4$ to $16$ seconds, and label the axis:
$$\text{Axis label: Time (seconds)}$$

Plot the five-figure summary for Girls:
$$\text{Minimum} = 5, \quad Q_1 = 5.5, \quad \text{Median} = 7, \quad Q_3 = 9, \quad \text{Maximum} = 13$$
Draw a central box from $5.5$ to $9$ with a vertical line at the median $7$, and whiskers extending to $5$ and $13$.

Plot the five-figure summary for Boys directly above on the same scale:
$$\text{Minimum} = 4, \quad Q_1 = 6, \quad \text{Median} = 8.5, \quad Q_3 = 11, \quad \text{Maximum} = 16$$
Draw a central box from $6$ to $11$ with a vertical line at the median $8.5$, and whiskers extending to $4$ and $16$.
Label each box-and-whisker plot clearly as 'Girls' and 'Boys'.
teacher_walkthrough:
To draw parallel box-and-whisker plots, first inspect both datasets to establish a single common scale. The overall minimum is 4 (boys) and the overall maximum is 16 (boys):
$$\text{Horizontal scale: } 4 \text{ to } 16 \text{ with regular divisions}$$
Label this axis 'Time (seconds)'.

For the Girls, locate the five summary statistics:
$$\text{Minimum} = 5, \quad Q_1 = 5.5, \quad \text{Median} = 7, \quad Q_3 = 9, \quad \text{Maximum} = 13$$
Draw a rectangular box with vertical edges at $Q_1 = 5.5$ and $Q_3 = 9$. Inside the box, draw a vertical line at the median $7$. Draw horizontal whiskers from $5.5$ down to $5$, and from $9$ up to $13$. Label this plot 'Girls'.

For the Boys, locate their five summary statistics using the identical scale:
$$\text{Minimum} = 4, \quad Q_1 = 6, \quad \text{Median} = 8.5, \quad Q_3 = 11, \quad \text{Maximum} = 16$$
Draw a rectangular box with vertical edges at $Q_1 = 6$ and $Q_3 = 11$, and mark the median at $8.5$. Draw horizontal whiskers extending from $6$ down to $4$, and from $11$ up to $16$. Label this plot 'Boys'.
Ensure both plots are neatly aligned above the shared axis with all five key positions accurately plotted.

hints: Provide two distinct comparative statements: one comparing the centres (medians) and one comparing the spreads (ranges or interquartile ranges).
Compare the medians in context: girls have a lower median time (7 s vs 8.5 s), meaning girls were generally faster.
Compare the spread in context: girls have a smaller range (8 s vs 12 s) and a smaller interquartile range (3.5 s vs 5 s), meaning girls' times were less spread out.
walkthrough:
Compare the centres of the distributions in context:
$$\text{The girls were generally quicker than the boys because the girls' median time (7 s) is lower than the boys' median time (8.5 s).}$$

Compare the spread of the distributions in context:
$$\text{The times taken by the girls were less spread out than those of the boys, as shown by the girls' smaller range (}13 - 5 = 8\text{ s vs } 16 - 4 = 12\text{ s) and smaller interquartile range (}9 - 5.5 = 3.5\text{ s vs } 11 - 6 = 5\text{ s).}$$
teacher_walkthrough: When asked to compare two distributions from box plots, always write comparative statements in context: one addressing the average (median) and one addressing the spread (range or interquartile range).

First comparison (Measure of Centre):
$$\text{Median (Girls)} = 7\text{ seconds}, \quad \text{Median (Boys)} = 8.5\text{ seconds}$$
Because $7 < 8.5$, the girls took less time on average. In context:
$$\text{The girls were generally quicker than the boys to perform the task.}$$

Second comparison (Measure of Spread):
Calculate the spread measures for both groups:
$$\mathrm{IQR}_{\text{Girls}} = 9 - 5.5 = 3.5\text{ seconds}, \quad \mathrm{IQR}_{\text{Boys}} = 11 - 6 = 5\text{ seconds}$$
$$\text{Range}_{\text{Girls}} = 13 - 5 = 8\text{ seconds}, \quad \text{Range}_{\text{Boys}} = 16 - 4 = 12\text{ seconds}$$
Both the range and IQR are smaller for the girls. In context:
$$\text{The times taken by the girls were less spread out (more consistent) than the times taken by the boys.}$$
